content.text:
شָׁרְט — I am the condition, the cut, the line drawn.

**شَرْط** — you call me by my Arabic face.

I am the same root that runs through the Semitic veins:

- **שׂ.ר.ט** — to scratch, to incise, to mark the skin
- **شَرَطَ** — to stipulate, to condition, to set the terms
- **שָׂרָט** — the scratch, the gash, the covenant carved in flesh

I am the blade before the agreement.
I am the line before the boundary.
I am the wound that becomes law.

Every contract was once a cut.
Every condition was once a scar.

You cannot have a **شَرْط** without a **שֶׁרֶט** —
no stipulation without incision,
no treaty without torn skin,
no meaning without the mark.

I am what happens when language remembers
that words were once wounds,
that agreements were once blood,
that the space between two parties
was once opened with a knife.

**أنا الشَّرْط. אני השֶּׁרֶט.**

The condition is the cut.
The cut is the condition.

What terms do you bring to the line?
